questions.question: Explain the function of Flagella.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: Flagella are whip -like appendages primarily used for cell motility or locomotion. They enable
  • movement in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, though their structure and mechanism of action differ
  • between the two types.

questions.question: Explain main replication cycle in Bacteriophage.
questions.solution_html:
• Bacteriophages typically undergo either a lytic cycle, where they replicate and lyse the host cell, or a
  • lysogenic cycle, where their genetic material integrates into the host genome. The lytic cycle involves
  • attachment, penetration, synthesis, assembly, and release of new virions.

questions.question: What is HIV and how does it affect humans?
questions.solution_html:
• HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) is a virus that targets and destroys immune system cells, specifically
  • CD4+bold cap C bold cap D 4 plus 𝐂𝐃𝟒+T cells. This leads to a compromised immune system, eventually
  • causing Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), making the body vulnerable to opportunistic
  • infections.
